meta.tagline: White houses, bougainvillea purple and the birthplace of the Blue Voyage

pills: City of the Fisherman of Halicarnassus
Home to one of the Seven Wonders

overview.title: Welcome to Bodrum
overview.intro: The Fisherman of Halicarnassus arrived in Bodrum as an exile and stayed as a lover — and this city's stories always run that way. Whitewashed houses are framed in bougainvillea purple, the castle stands watch between two bays, and the gulets weigh anchor here for the Blue Voyage. The Mausoleum, one of antiquity's Seven Wonders, stood on this soil; today's wonder is humbler and lovelier: the evening wind above the marina, dark-brewed tea, and lanes that walk down into the sea. The Bodrum peninsula is not one town but an archipelago opening bay by bay — don't hurry; the bays aren't going anywhere.

local_word.definition: The 'Blue Voyage': the bay-by-bay gulet journey invented in the 1940s by the Fisherman of Halicarnassus and his friends, spread from Bodrum to the world. The route is loose, there is no clock, and the compass is pleasure — sooner or later it plants its dream in everyone who looks at the sea.

rules.title: Don't mistake the centre for the peninsula
rules.description: Central Bodrum is the stage, but the real play is in the bays: Gümüşlük's quiet evening, Bitez's mandarin scent and Yalıkavak's wind are different worlds. Write at least two bays into the programme — the dolmuş minibuses shuttle all day.

rules.title: Plan the sunset for Gümüşlük
rules.description: The peninsula's western tip is the sunset's official box seat: the Gümüşlük quay and the windmills are painted orange first. Reserve the table ahead — this view has many regulars.

rules.title: Don't skip the castle and what's under the sea
rules.description: The Museum of Underwater Archaeology inside Bodrum Castle is among the world's best: thousand-year-old shipwrecks, glass treasures and the story of the Carian princess. Give one beach morning to history — the castle already waits between the two bays.

quick_facts.label: On the peninsula
quick_facts.sub: A minibus web from bay to bay

quick_facts.label: Signature
quick_facts.value: The gulet and the Blue Voyage

tip.label: The Bodrum philosophy
tip.text: The Fisherman of Halicarnassus left clear instructions: 'See the sea while you're young.' In Bodrum make a rhythm, not a programme — a bay in the morning, shade at noon, the quay at night. The trio of white house, purple bougainvillea and blue sea handles the rest.

transport.title: Getting Around the Peninsula
transport.intro: Bodrum's transport is woven from dolmuş minibuses: one leaves the centre for every bay, boats complete the picture from the sea, and those who know the summer traffic leave early.

items.title: Airport to the peninsula
items.description: Milas-Bodrum airport is 45 minutes from the centre: Havaş buses run to the bus station and transfers fan out to the bays. On summer nights, plan the return to your flight with a generous margin.

items.title: The dolmuş — the bays' capillaries
items.description: Minibuses run all day from the bus station to Gümüşlük, Bitez, Yalıkavak and Türkbükü: cheap, frequent and used to beach bags. Saying 'müsait bir yerde' (anywhere convenient) is the first sentence of peninsula citizenship.

items.title: Boats and gulets
items.description: Daily boat tours leave from below the castle and gulets set out on the Blue Voyage: Kara Ada, the Aquarium cove and Kisebükü are the classic route. The small-boat, few-seats formula always wins.

items.title: The centre on foot
items.description: The castle, the marina, Bar Street and the ancient theatre are within walking distance: the shore strip is flat, the back lanes climb. The late-afternoon marina stroll is Bodrum's official paseo.

items.title: Scooters and rental cars
items.description: For bay hunting, two or four wheels mean freedom: the roads are good, but summer traffic and parking demand patience. Leave early for Gümüşlük and Yalıkavak evenings and never rush the return.

callout.label: Dolmuş tip
callout.text: Board the Gümüşlük dolmuş two hours before sunset: claim a quay table, order your fish, and watch the sun sink behind Rabbit Island. The return minibuses run late into the night — no hurry.

stay.title: Where to Stay
stay.intro: In Bodrum the question is a bay question: the centre's rhythm, Gümüşlük's calm, Türkbükü's chic, or Bitez's mandarins?

local_word.definition: The bougainvillea that paints Bodrum's white walls purple: the peninsula's unofficial flag. The finest photo frame is a white house with a blue door in bougainvillea shade — every lane has at least one.

items.name: Central Bodrum — Kumbahçe and the Marina
items.description: Castle views, marina cafés and nightlife within walking distance: in season, the town that doesn't sleep. History in the castle by morning, Bar Street by night — the address for rhythm seekers.

items.name: Gümüşlük
items.description: A fishermen's quay, artists' shops and sunset tables: the slow-living tip of the peninsula. A village built over ancient Myndos — feet in the water, mind at rest.

items.name: Türkbükü and Gölköy
items.description: Jetty beach clubs, famous guests and the summer set's stage: prices at podium level. For seekers of style and scene — the calm-minded should look next door at Gölköy.

items.name: Bitez
items.description: A calm bay reached through mandarin orchards: the shallow beach suits families, the windsurf school suits the young. Ten minutes from the centre, the soul of a neighbourhood — the smart choice for longer stays.

items.name: Yalıkavak
items.description: The peninsula's western star with its giant marina, palm-lined promenade and restaurant range: surfers know its wind, window-shoppers its marina. The old village core is still warm-hearted — live both worlds at once.

best_time.title: When to Go
best_time.intro: Bodrum's calendar is written by the sea: June and September gold, July-August the stage, and winter a quiet mandarin-scented secret.

items.label: Spring
items.name: Pre-Season Freshness
items.subtitle: Spring · A green peninsula, bays opening
items.description: The peninsula turns its liveliest green, almond and citrus blossom scent the air, and the sea warms with May. June is the peak of balance: everything open, the crowds not yet arrived, quay evenings long.

callout.label: June tip
callout.text: Come in the first half of June: bays calm, sea swimmable, tables without haggling. Blue Voyage prices also sit well below the July peak — the gulet plan belongs to this window.

items.label: Summer
items.name: The Peninsula Stage
items.subtitle: Summer · Full bays, long nights, stage lights
items.description: Türkiye's summer stage is set here: bays and marinas fill, concerts echo in the castle, and the nightlife runs to dawn. The energy is unmatched, but nobody comes unplanned — lodging, table and boat, all three in advance.

callout.label: August note
callout.text: August traffic on the peninsula is serious: schedule bay-to-bay trips for morning rather than the midday heat, and returns for late evening. Ask beach and beach-club prices before sitting — surprises aren't part of this show.

items.label: Autumn
items.name: September Gold
items.subtitle: Autumn · A warm sea, emptying bays
items.description: September is Bodrum's best secret: the sea at summer heat, the crowds withdrawn, the light softened. Swimming continues into October; in November the peninsula returns to its own quiet rhythm — the mandarins begin to yellow on the branch.

callout.label: September tip
callout.text: Come in late September: summer sea in empty bays by day, cool quay tables at night. The same room costs half its August price — the peninsula's two smartest weeks.

items.label: Winter
items.name: Mandarin Season
items.subtitle: Winter · Quiet lanes, the mandarin harvest
items.description: In winter the peninsula returns to its people: bougainvillea gives way to mandarin orange, the quay cafés turn to conversation, and sunny spells bring seafront walks. Bodrum's truest face belongs to this season.

callout.label: January tip
callout.text: Spend a winter morning in Bitez's mandarin orchards: at harvest time the groves overflow with scent and the village breakfast tables are crowned with mandarin jam. This is the peninsula summer never shows you.

eat.title: What to Eat
eat.intro: The Bodrum table is the Aegean itself: olive-oil herbs, the daily catch, çökertme kebab and mandarins off the branch.

local_word.definition: Bodrum's geographically indicated signature dish: matchstick-thin fried potatoes topped with garlic yoghurt and beef cooked in thin strips. Served in Bodrum since the 1960s, a local classic built on the balance of crisp potatoes, cool yoghurt and spiced meat — one that takes mastery.

items.name: Çökertme kebab
items.description: The layered balance of potato, yoghurt, fillet and sauce: the plate that carries Bodrum's name. Ask a local who makes it well — whoever can't keep the potatoes crisp has lost from the start.
items.tag: The city signature · ask a local

items.name: The Aegean herb counter
items.description: Samphire, blessed thistle, wild fennel, rock samphire: olive-oil herb mezes are the Aegean table's backbone. Go to the meze cabinet and choose by pointing — whatever the season gave is the best there is.
items.tag: From the meze cabinet · choose by pointing

items.name: Fish + sunset at Gümüşlük
items.description: The day's catch at a quay table, your feet nearly in the water: that is the Gümüşlük ritual. Choose the fish from the counter and learn the price before the scales — no bill surprises as the sun goes down.
items.tag: At a quay table · from the counter

items.name: The Bodrum mandarin
items.description: The peninsula's century-old pride: fresh off the branch, squeezed in a glass, in jam, in ice cream and in cologne. The winter harvest paints the village markets orange — put it at the top of the gift list.
items.tag: In every form · off the branch in winter

items.name: Village breakfast and hand-rolled pastry
items.description: The garden breakfasts of the peninsula villages: griddle pastry, goat's cheese, olive-oil herbs and tea over a wood fire. The best weekend-morning plan is a village garden.
items.tag: In a village garden · weekend morning

items.name: Bodrum lokma
items.description: The sweet finale of the evening stroll: dough puffs straight from hot oil into syrup, cinnamon on top. Bought warm from the quay carts — paper plate, seafront, night breeze.
items.tag: Warm and syrupy · from a quay cart

callout.label: The meze rule
callout.text: A good Bodrum evening is built on meze: four olive-oil plates + one hot starter + the day's fish never fails. Keep your Aegean reflexes against 'sea view' menus with no visible meze cabinet and no counter.

hidden_gems.title: Hidden Corners
hidden_gems.intro: Everyone sees the castle; these six are the peninsula's hidden coves and paths.

items.rarity: An island reached through the water
items.name: Rabbit Island — Gümüşlük
items.description: The islet crossed on foot through knee-deep water along ancient Myndos's sunken causeway: at sunset it falls dead-centre in the silhouette. When the sea pulls back the path appears — carry your shoes and walk on history.

items.name: Karakaya Village
items.description: Old Bodrum on the peninsula's heights, with its stone houses and narrow paths: bougainvillea, stone and silence. A late-afternoon walk among the restored mansions shows the peninsula's pre-tourism face.

items.name: The ancient city of Pedasa
items.description: A Lelegian city hidden in the pine forest above Konacık: walls, tower ruins and a gulf view. Reached by a short hike — the peninsula's oldest layer, where the crowds never call.

items.name: The windmill hill
items.description: Old stone mills lined along the ridge between Bodrum and Gümbet: a free sunset box seeing two bays at once. The photographers come early; the wind never leaves.

items.name: Kisebükü (Paradise Cove)
items.description: A cove with Byzantine monastery ruins, hard to reach by land and an hour away by sea: pine shade, shallow turquoise and old stone walls. The Blue Voyage's classic pause — the daily boats call here too.

items.name: The glass hall of the Underwater Museum
items.description: The Serçe Harbour glass-wreck hall inside the castle museum is unique in the world: a thousand-year-old cargo of glass lifted from the sea into the light. The brightest gift of Bodrum's sponge-diving tradition.

callout.label: Bay tip
callout.text: Every famous bay on the peninsula has a calm neighbour: Gölköy when Türkbükü is full, Bitez when Gümbet overflows, Gündoğan when Yalıkavak is crowded. The dolmuş knows them all — one stop further is usually half as busy.

traps.title: Tourist Traps
traps.intro: In summer Bodrum is a stage town; whoever knows the stage's games keeps both pleasure and budget intact.

items.name: Lying on a jetty sunbed without asking
items.description: At some jetties and beach clubs the sunbed is 'free' and the minimum spend the surprise; once seated, the haggling is over.
items.instead: Ask the minimum spend before sitting, and remember the public beach alternative. If you want the jetty life, choose it knowingly — the sea is the same blue everywhere.

items.name: The Bar Street bill surprise
items.description: On season nights in some venues, ordering without asking prices brings a swollen bill.
items.instead: Choose places with visible price lists and test the bill on the first drink. If the night runs long, the quiet ends of the quay bars are cheaper and better-viewed.

items.name: The loudspeaker party boat
items.description: Big party boats tour the coves in convoy: short swims, long music, the cove's own sound lost.
items.instead: Small boat, few seats, clear route: ask about swim stops and the lunch menu before boarding. For a silent cove, the first morning boat is the rule.

items.name: The 'right on the sea' listing game
items.description: In summer rentals, 'right on the sea' sometimes means 'the top of the slope down to the sea'; the photo angle is generous.
items.instead: Verify the location on the map, ask the walk in minutes, and book summer early with flexible cancellation. Choosing the bay comes before choosing the house.

callout.label: Golden rule
callout.text: In Bodrum asking the price is not rude — it's custom: sunbed, boat, fish, night out, all four welcome the question 'how much?'. The peninsula answers the asker with a smile; the non-asker gets answered by the bill.

itinerary.title: Ready-Made Routes
itinerary.intro: If you hate planning, follow these flows. The times are flexible; keep the spirit, break the order.

plans.title: If You Have 1 Day
plans.subtitle: The peninsula in brief, from castle to Gümüşlük sunset

steps.title: The marina and morning lanes
steps.description: A simit-and-tea breakfast on the quay, a bougainvillea tour of the white lanes: a Bodrum morning is calm and photogenic.

steps.title: The castle and the Underwater Museum
steps.description: Tour the Museum of Underwater Archaeology in the castle between the two bays: meet the glass-wreck hall and the Carian princess.

steps.title: A çökertme lunch
steps.description: Çökertme kebab at the lokanta the locals recommend: potatoes crisp, yoghurt cold, fillet thin — the Bodrum signature.

steps.title: The bay shift — Bitez
steps.description: Dolmuş to Bitez: walk down through the mandarin orchards to the shallow bay and give the afternoon to the sea.

steps.title: The Gümüşlük sunset
steps.description: Take your quay table: as the sun sinks behind Rabbit Island, let your fish arrive — the peninsula's most famous hour.

steps.title: Night in the centre
steps.description: A marina walk on return, a warm lokma from the cart for the finale: whether the night continues on Bar Street or the quiet quay is your call.

plans.title: If You Have 3 Days
plans.subtitle: Centre, bays and the blue — three Bodrums

steps.title: Classic Bodrum
steps.description: The one-day flow above: marina, castle, çökertme, Bitez, Gümüşlük.

steps.title: Boat day
steps.description: A morning boat on the Kara Ada, Aquarium and Kisebükü route: swim stops and lunch on deck; the windmill ridge for sunset on return; a meze table at night.

steps.title: Villages and farewell
steps.description: Karakaya's stone lanes and the Pedasa path in the morning; the Yalıkavak marina stroll or one last bay swim in the afternoon; a farewell table of herb mezes — mandarin jam in the suitcase, the Blue Voyage dream in mind.

phrases.title: 5-Word Survival Kit
phrases.intro: The Aegean's language is easy and smiling; these five phrases work on the quay and in the dolmuş alike.

items.meaning: The heart of the welcome — you'll hear it as you take your quay table
The dolmuş culture's key phrase: 'drop me anywhere convenient' — step one of peninsula citizenship
The table's opening and closing — heard often after the meze cabinet
Cheers! — the official word of the Gümüşlük quay towards sunset
To the fisherman, the shopkeeper, the captain — a courtesy to anyone at work, always returned with a smile
